source_basis: Valentin-Silva et al. 2025 Ecology and Evolution / PMC12432336
notes: Selection is measured on floral traits and fruit-set fitness, but seed predators are invoked as a likely explanation for ovary-width selection rather than measured as a matched local antagonist component. Corolla traits were not significantly selected.

source_basis: Zu et al. 2016 New Phytologist DOI 10.1111/nph.13652
notes: Bidirectional artificial selection estimates volatile heritability and pleiotropic responses. Pollinator attraction and herbivore deterrence motivate the system but are not the focal measured consumer-mediated selection components.

source_basis: Sheppard et al. 2026 American Journal of Botany DOI 10.1002/ajb2.70167
notes: On the Nature of Things article proposes a fitness-landscape framework and illustration; it does not contribute a new empirical pollinator-antagonist trait-selection dataset.

source_basis: Snow et al. 2001 Ecological Applications DOI 10.1890/1051-0761(2001)011[0934:FOHBWA]2.0.CO;2
notes: Fitness comparison concerns wild versus crop-radish hybrids. Shared pollinators and possible future herbivore-resistance genes are not a measured pollinator-antagonist selection geometry on one floral trait.

source_basis: Walsh et al. 2022 Journal of Pollination Ecology DOI 10.26786/1920-7603(2022)685
notes: Honeycreepers robbed all visited banana-poka flowers; nectar standing crop and sugar composition were measured. Plant reproductive consequences were explicitly left for future research.

Individual-based mutualism-antagonism typologies predict reproductive success, but the estimand is interaction-network composition/strength rather than a repeated selection effect on one plant trait coordinate.

source_basis: Koranyi et al. 2026 Basic and Applied Ecology DOI 10.1016/j.baae.2026.07.005
notes: Fragmentation, floral resources, pollinator activity, leaf herbivory and dry fruit mass are quantified, but no single plant trait coordinate carries the pollinator and antagonist selection components.

Bumblebees provide >90% of pollination service while long-tongued butterflies/moths act as nectar robbers across three Roscoea species; this is repeated role/service ecology, not a final-fitness trait-selection estimand.
